card.title: Food Chain, Food Web and Ecological Pyramids

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Energy moves through ecosystems in food chains — grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk — or, more realistically, in food webs of interlocking chains that buffer species loss. Lindeman's ten percent law governs every step: ~90% of energy is lost as heat, so chains stay short and top predators rare.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Food chain: Producer (TL1) → Primary consumer (TL2) → Secondary consumer (TL3) → Tertiary consumer (TL4)
10% rule: only ~10% of energy transfers between trophic levels
GPP = total photosynthesis; NPP = GPP − plant respiration (R)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **GPP vs NPP:** GPP = total fixed; NPP = GPP − respiration = what's actually stored and available.  ·  **Standing crop vs productivity:** standing crop = biomass at an instant (snapshot); productivity = rate of production over time (movie).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the three ecological pyramids and when each can be inverted.  ·  The 10% rule and the always-upright energy pyramid are very common exam points.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Grassland chain*** — grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk.  ·  ***Banyan-inversion*** — one tree, many insects: inverted number pyramid.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: food chain, food web, trophic level, ecological pyramids (within Ecology).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Biology — don't mix them.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Define trophic level. **Answer.** The **position an organism occupies in a food chain**, decided by its source of energy: T1 producers, T2 primary consumers (herbivores), T3 secondary consumers (carnivores), T4 tertiary consumers/top carnivores.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Energy flows, matter cycles:** energy enters once and leaves as heat (one-way); nutrients cycle indefinitely — the fundamental asymmetry that makes ecosystems depend on constant solar input.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Food chain: linear energy path; grazing vs detritus; trophic levels T1–T5; 10% law (Lindeman) → chains short, top predators rare.  ·  Food web: interlocking chains — stable, realistic.  ·  Pyramids: numbers (invert: tree-insects), biomass (invert: ocean phytoplankton), energy (always upright — heat lost one-way).  ·  NPP = GPP − R; units kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹. 2022 numerical: 4800 − 1200 = 3600.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Roughly 1% of sunlight reaching Earth is converted to biomass by photosynthesis.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — How Energy Moves Through Life Every ecosystem runs on one currency: energy, entering as sunlight and leaving as heat, passing from plants to herbivores to carnivores. Food chains and webs trace that flow; pyramids depict it; productivity measures it. This topic carries more NEB questions than any other in ecology — including a numerical.  ·  ## 2. Food Chain, Food Web and Trophic Levels ### 2.1 Food chain — the linear energy path **Grazing food chain (starts with living plants):** Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk (Producer → Primary consumer → Secondary → Tertiary → Top carnivore) **Detritus food chain (starts with dead matter):** Dead leaves → Detritivores (earthworm, woodlice) → Decomposer…  ·  ## 3. Ecological Pyramids (NEB 2024 + 2023) **Definition:** graphical representation of a trophic parameter (number, biomass, energy) with producers at the base and top carnivores at the apex. | Pyramid | Base → apex | Usually upright? | Can invert? | |---|---|---|---| | **Pyramid of numbers** | Count of individuals | Usually | **Yes** — one big tree supports thousands of…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pyramid of energy: always upright; each level < the one below  ·  **Grazing vs detritus chain:** grazing starts with living plants; detritus starts with dead organic matter — in forests the detritus chain dominates.  ·  NPP = GPP − respiration is a calculation question.

Eating grain directly puts a person at T2 and harvests ~10× more energy per hectare than eating grain-fed animals, which puts the person at T3.…
